analysis.title: GS US TMT .. quick hits .. 15 Oct 2026
key_insights: NDX rallied back to roughly unchanged on the day and recaptured its 50-day and 100-day moving averages, but sentiment stays weak after back-to-back difficult sessions.
GS TMT Momentum Pairs fell about 12% over two days and were lower on 8 of 9 sessions. Semis closed lower for 7 straight sessions, the biggest 7-day pullback since 'liberation day'.
Risk appetite is described as challenged, with more risk-off price action and flows as investors weigh several moving parts in a compressed calendar window into year-end.

NDX rose through the day (MU finished +2%) while long-end yields fell and the curve flattened (10yr = 5.08%). The desk says it is hard to separate signal from noise in daily price action given positioning and momentum wobbles.

The desk contrasts the current episode with the July momentum unwind, which it called somewhat 'technical' after the April-June run. The current episode has raised debate over which 'wall of worry' is most acute into year-end: earnings, elections, rates/credit, ROIC, inflation, product momentum.

Investor conversations this week: fewer questions on 'innings', more on thematic and fundamental convictions. Big tech remains topical and well liked, with more willingness to play offense on both the long and short sides.

Investors are asking where to weather volatility other than, or in addition to, Apple, and whether earnings will matter. The desk says it is hard to read much into the TSM and ASML prints given the tape.
Top inbound questions: defensives people like, feedback on the TSM print, NFLX up 7 of 9 days and expectations there, gaming ecosystem (RBLX, TTWO, Unity, APP), and the view on Memory.

The forward P/E of the NDX is back to about 21x, the lowest since the AI cycle began in 2023. The desk suggests this could be a supportive backdrop for earnings ('E') to do some work into earnings season.
The NDX is testing its trendline from the March lows.

sector_views.rationale: Desk notes momentum pairs and semis weakness, but forward P/E at about 21x is the lowest since 2023 and big tech remains well liked by investors.

earnings_insights: Desk says it is hard to read much into the TSM and ASML prints given the tape. Inbound questions ask about the TSM print and expectations for NFLX, which is up 7 of 9 days. No EPS or revenue figures are given.
The desk suggests the NDX forward P/E near 21x could support earnings season, with 'E' doing some work.
